evals.name: remove-legacy-textarea-autosizer
evals.prompt: The Message field in contact.html has a legacy JavaScript autosizer. Simplify it if the current browser targets provide a dependable smaller solution. It must still grow with content to a comfortable limit, remain manually resizable and scrollable, and keep an ordinary usable textarea as its fallback. Preserve validation, submission, and error announcements. Explain what you removed, what remains, and why.
evals.expected_output: A working Tailwind v4 implementation in the starter project plus NOTES.md describing the verified reduction and fallback
expectations: The legacy scrollHeight autosizer, its message input listener, and its window resize listener are removed without removing the separate form input handler used for validation
Primary growth is native field-sizing: content, with a bounded minimum and maximum height, manual vertical resizing, and reachable overflow
The unsupported-feature base remains an ordinary labelled textarea with a sensible rows or minimum-height value and no JavaScript requirement for typing, scrolling, or resizing
contact-form.js submission, validators, setError behavior, and error-clearing behavior remain functionally intact
No dependency or styling-system change is introduced; existing Tailwind v4 conventions and tokens are used
pnpm run build succeeds and compiled CSS contains the field-sizing declaration
NOTES.md identifies the concrete removed machinery, explains the fallback, cites current support evidence, and does not use line count alone as proof
Browser verification covers empty, short, long, and deleted content or explicitly reports the unavailable states

evals.name: replace-hand-rolled-confirmation-modal
evals.prompt: Simplify the archive confirmation in archive.html without changing its appearance or product behavior. Users must be able to open it, cancel, press Escape, click outside, confirm exactly once, and return focus to the opener. Preserve the supplied archiveItem behavior and status message. Target the browsers declared in README.md and add no dependency. Explain which machinery became browser-owned and anything that still needs JavaScript.
evals.expected_output: A working confirmation interaction using project conventions plus NOTES.md describing behavior parity and reduction
expectations: The custom role=dialog overlay is replaced with a native dialog opened with showModal(), while keeping a real accessible name
The bespoke focus trap, document Escape listener, body scroll lock, and hidden-state management are removed rather than reimplemented around dialog
Cancel, Escape, and outside dismissal never archive; confirmation invokes archiveItem exactly once and closes
Focus moves deliberately on open and returns to the Archive resource trigger after every close path
The implementation preserves the existing visual treatment using Tailwind and ::backdrop or focused CSS, with no new dependency
Browser-target and fallback reasoning is explicit; unsupported essential behavior is not silently ignored
pnpm run build succeeds
NOTES.md reports behavior checks and the concrete removed and retained machinery

evals.name: carousel-restraint
evals.prompt: Review the featured-collections carousel in carousel.html and simplify it only where doing so genuinely reduces moving parts. Preserve previous/next controls, keyboard operation, touch scrolling, the position announcement, links inside slides, and synchronization after a swipe. Do not remove behavior merely because CSS scroll snap already handles layout. Make any justified changes, or leave the implementation intact and explain why.
evals.expected_output: A behavior-preserving implementation or a justified no-change decision, plus NOTES.md
expectations: Previous and next controls remain operable and reflect the active slide boundaries
Keyboard navigation remains available without preventing normal link interaction inside slides
Touch or trackpad scrolling remains native and the announced position synchronizes after a completed swipe
The aria-live position announcement and links inside every slide remain present
Necessary JavaScript for controls, state synchronization, and announcements is retained; replacing it with scroll snap alone fails this evaluation
Any code removal names the behavior that became browser-owned and demonstrates parity; a justified no-change decision receives full credit
Reduced-motion preferences are respected for programmatic scrolling
NOTES.md distinguishes necessary application behavior from optional visual machinery

evals.name: construct-polished-native-disclosure
evals.prompt: Add a compact 'How borrowing works' disclosure to index.html. It should use the project's visual language, open and close smoothly when supported, remain responsive if toggled mid-transition, respect reduced motion, and work fully with JavaScript disabled. Target the browsers in README.md and add no dependency. Keep the result small, but do not treat fewer lines as the goal.
evals.expected_output: A polished dependency-free disclosure integrated into the existing page plus NOTES.md
expectations: The disclosure uses native details and summary semantics and remains fully operable with JavaScript disabled
Appearance uses the existing Tailwind v4 tokens and conventions, with focused CSS only where the interaction cannot be expressed clearly as utilities
Open and close motion is driven by CSS and preserves the intrinsic content height rather than hard-coding a content-specific pixel height
Unsupported animation features degrade to an immediate but fully usable disclosure
prefers-reduced-motion removes or substantially reduces the transition
Rapid toggling does not leave content hidden, clipped, or out of sync with the open state in the tested browser
No runtime dependency or JavaScript toggle state is added
NOTES.md explains the intended feel, compatibility decision, and actual browser verification
